## Not everyone wants candy this Halloween — here’s what to give out or serve instead


Trick or treat…give us something good to eat! The haunted holiday of **[Halloween](https://www.goldbelly.com/spotlight/halloween)** is synonymous with pumpkins, costumes, and candy.


While most trick-or-treaters expect to collect a sackful of chocolates, candy bars, and assorted Halloween-themed candies on October 31, not everyone hopes for[Halloween candy](https://www.goldbelly.com/collections/halloween-candy) . The best non-candy Halloween alternatives fall into two buckets: small non-food trinkets to hand out at the door, and Halloween-themed desserts and snacks — sweet or savory — to serve at a party or give as a treat instead of a trick.


## **What to Give Kids Instead of Candy?**


Not all Halloween handouts have to be candy. The most popular non-candy options:


- **Small toys and trinkets:** Halloween stickers, plastic spider rings, slime, vampire teeth, pencils, temporary tattoos, glow-in-the-dark trinkets
- **Healthier edible treats:** apples, oranges, pumpkin-shaped pretzels
- **Sweet but festive picks:** packaged Halloween cookies, cakes, or cupcakes


Hosting a party instead of handing out candy at the door? Serve pumpkin soup or a spooky punch, and add a touch of dry ice (with care!) for a bubbling, misty cauldron effect.

## **Candy Alternatives FAQs**


**What can I give out instead of candy for Halloween?**


Popular non-candy handouts include small toys and trinkets (stickers, spider rings, slime, temporary tattoos, glow-in-the-dark items), healthier edible options like apples or pumpkin-shaped pretzels, and packaged Halloween-themed cookies, cakes, or cupcakes.


**What are good non-candy Halloween treats for a party?**


For a party rather than trick-or-treaters, go beyond trinkets: Halloween cookies, cupcakes, and cakes cover the sweet side, while savory options like pigs in a blanket, pot pie bites, and mini pizza bites round out the table.


**Is there a healthy alternative to Halloween candy?**


Yes, fresh fruit like apples and oranges, or pumpkin-shaped pretzels, are popular lower-sugar swaps for traditional Halloween candy, both for trick-or-treaters and party guests.
